stories.delivered_paragraph: Elon Musk’s xAI, now owned by SpaceX, sued Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison to block a state law banning tools that generate non-consensual sexualized images. The statute, due to take effect Saturday, permits fines of $500,000 for each explicit deepfake a user creates; xAI says it is an overbroad, content-based restriction on speech. Minnesota’s defense will test how far states can go in regulating AI image generators without violating First Amendment protections.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Federal Communications Commission announced an import ban on foreign-made “advanced robotic devices” and power inverters, including mobile humanoid and quadruped robots. Although the agency did not name a country, the policy is expected to hit Chinese robot makers and major inverter suppliers such as Sungrow and already-blacklisted Huawei, citing what the FCC calls unacceptable risks. The move extends U.S. technology restrictions beyond chips and telecom equipment into robotics and renewable-energy supply chains.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Federal Aviation Administration is moving to waive some environmental rules for launch approvals, a change that could speed missions by SpaceX, Blue Origin and other U.S. space companies. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy framed the proposal as an effort to cut red tape and preserve America’s edge in a renewed space race. The practical question will be whether faster licensing can be achieved without weakening scrutiny of launches’ effects on surrounding communities and wildlife.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Senate Majority Leader John Thune and House Speaker Mike Johnson plan to attend President Trump’s two-day midterm convention in Dallas in September, joining a party gathering designed to project unity and draw major donors. The event forces Republicans in competitive races to weigh the fundraising benefits of appearing with Trump against political risks at home.

stories.delivered_paragraph: President Trump and the Justice Department separately asked the Supreme Court to overturn the $83.3 million defamation verdict won by writer E. Jean Carroll. Trump argues he was immune because his 2019 denials of Carroll’s sexual-assault allegation were made while president; the DOJ says the federal government should have replaced him as defendant, which would have ended the case. The petitions seek to broaden protections for presidents and federal employees over statements made in office.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Senate voted 86-12 to advance a Russia and Iran sanctions bill previously championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, shortly after lawmakers met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The proposal would impose 100% secondary tariffs on countries buying Russian oil and gas, target Moscow’s tanker “shadow fleet,” and renew expiring Iran sanctions. The overwhelming procedural vote gives leaders room to seek faster final passage despite earlier White House concerns.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Mexican drug cartels are increasingly shifting methamphetamine production activity toward Nigeria, part of a broader effort to exploit West Africa’s growing role in illicit-drug manufacturing and export, the BBC reports. The development would extend cartel-linked supply chains far beyond their traditional base and take advantage of routes connecting Africa to overseas markets. It also raises the enforcement burden for Nigerian and regional authorities confronting a more internationalized synthetic-drug trade.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Eric McCormack has joined the cast of “You’re Safe Now,” a psychological thriller directed by Nimisha Mukerji and written by Jess Mastro, with production underway in Toronto. stories.delivered_paragraph: Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” is expected to pass the $330 million domestic lifetime total of “Oppenheimer” on its 13th day in theaters, compared with 595 days for Nolan’s 2023 hit. Its second Monday brought in $14.7 million, lifting the running U.S. total to about $320.1 million, while “Hadestown” earned $2.2 million that day. The rapid run would make “The Odyssey” Nolan’s third-highest-grossing domestic release, before its next test against a new “Spider-Man” film.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Ariana Grande sued unidentified hackers in Los Angeles Superior Court, alleging they stole and sold or posted unreleased music, videos and photos online. The complaint says 45 unreleased songs were leaked in 2023 alone and that hundreds of leaks have occurred since her 2011 debut, including masters, demos and recording-session footage. The suit seeks to identify the defendants and halt distribution of material whose leaks can undermine an artist’s control over releases and commercial plans.

stories.delivered_paragraph: FIFA is considering selling minority stakes in commercial rights connected to the World Cup to raise billions of dollars, including through a firm run by Joshua Kushner, brother of Jared Kushner, NPR reports. It could reshape how World Cup income is financed and distributed, prompting scrutiny from national and regional football bodies.

stories.delivered_paragraph: UEFA will hold an emergency meeting to discuss possible resistance, including a potential World Cup boycott, to FIFA’s plan to raise $20 billion by selling equity to outside investors, ESPN reported. European football’s governing body is objecting to a proposal that could give private investors a stake in World Cup commercial rights. Even the prospect of a boycott underscores how a financial restructuring could trigger a confrontation between FIFA and the confederation representing many of the sport’s strongest teams.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Ford shares rose after the automaker matched General Motors in relying on pickup trucks and other traditionally powered vehicles to limit a sales decline. The result highlights how demand for higher-margin combustion-engine models remains important to Detroit carmakers even as they spend heavily on electric vehicles. Investors welcomed the evidence that Ford can protect sales through its established truck franchise, but the company still faces the longer-term challenge of balancing that strength with its EV transition.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Saudi Arabia is increasing loadings through a Mediterranean port to reach oil buyers by a longer, more expensive route, MarketWatch reports. The workaround is intended to keep exports moving even though the alternative route adds transport costs and complexity. For crude markets, the shift illustrates how regional security and logistics disruptions can raise the cost of supplying customers without necessarily cutting Saudi production, potentially supporting prices and narrowing trading margins.
